brief: THE BET — take the swing; a 150-300 line diff is expected and welcome. The town holds 75 people on a summer afternoon, every one of them on an errand that ends in a stop that performs something and usually says it (sayAt, 37 sites). The observer can NAME any of them under the pointer and can go to five fixed quarters — and the camera has never once been pointed at something that moves. Click a person and the frame takes them: it eases onto them at a readable zoom, keeps them in the picture as they walk, tells you in the ticker who they are and what they are doing, and lets go — easing back where you came from — when their errand ends, when they leave the world, or when you click away. A visitor who clicks once learns in ten seconds that this is a town of individuals with somewhere to be, which no amount of staring at the wide shot will teach them. A quarter is DATA (QUARTERS is a list of boxes with air/keep/share that viewFor fits), so the cheapest honest shape for a follow is a box that MOVES with its subject and leaves viewFor, inView and the ease working unchanged.
successLooksLike: On a desktop at Wide, clicking a walker eases the frame onto them; they stay in the picture for the whole of their errand while the town carries on around them; the ticker names them and their stop as it happens; the follow releases cleanly on any of the three exits and eases back. frame-cost.mjs shows no new per-frame ground rebuild, and the ordinary Wide frame is unchanged when nothing is being followed.
avoid: THE GROUND CACHE IS THE WHOLE RISK, and whereGo has already solved it once: an ease survives only because it paints the padded WIDE cache once (groundPad/gpadWant/gview), scales the blit by `k = viewS/gview.s`, and repaints the destination ONCE on arrival. drawGround costs 25-27 ms (c214), so a follow that sets groundDirty per frame drops every frame. Hold the padded wide cache for the whole follow and repaint once on release. FACES are registered in gview's frame and faceAt maps through the same k — keep that true. Do not exceed VIEW_SMAX or drop held()'s WORLD_X0/WORLD_X1 clamps, or the frame runs off the world into the cache's column repeat. Agents are transient: one whose route ends off the world must release the follow, never snap. Wide must stay exempt in inView and bit-identical while nothing is followed — the census and motion gates depend on it. No new R() draw: a click is not a seeded event. And do NOT fix the backdrop's stale horizon in here; that is b165's.
